newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia end-June palm oil stocks seen at 700,000t.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia end-June palm oil stocks seen at 700,000t.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil stocks are expected to total around 700,000 tonnes at end-June 1997 against 774,000 tonnes at end-June 1996, the U.S. embassy said.

"With anticipated increases in overseas demand in the next few months, the palm oil stock level is expected to hover around the 700,000 tonnes level during the April-June period," it said in a report released on Tuesday. It has also estimated end-March 1997 stocks at 690,000 tonnes.
Traders forecast end-March stocks at 710,000-725,000 tonnes.
The U.S. embassy said April-June output was estimated at 2.07 million tonnes versus 2.06 million tonnes in the same period the previous year.

"A seasonal uptrend is expected from the month of March and the industry is expecting crude palm oil production to increase 20 to 25 percent during March," the embassy added. Malaysian private crop forecaster Ivan Wong on Monday estimated March output would rise 32 percent from February to 663,000 tonnes. Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) will release official March crop data stock data on April 15. January-March output in 1997 was estimated at 1.71 million tonnes against 1.64 million tonnes in the same period of the 1996, the embassy added.
